Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The issue report indicates a NegativeArraySizeException occurs in the parsePaxHeaders method when there is an empty line at the end of the PAX headers. Inspecting the parsePaxHeaders method reveals that the method reads the length of the header line in a loop starting at line 456, where it reads characters and builds an integer length (len) from digits by subtracting '0' from the character and multiplying len by 10 each iteration (lines 494-495). However, if it encounters a newline character (ASCII 10) instead of a digit, subtracting '0' (ASCII 48) from it yields a negative value, causing len to become negative. Subsequently, when calculating restLen = len - read (line 470), restLen becomes negative. This length is used to allocate a byte array (line 474), resulting in the NegativeArraySizeException.

The method currently assumes every character up to the space is a valid digit forming the length field, but it does not check whether the character is actually a digit. This assumption fails if there is an empty line (represented by a newline character) where it incorrectly interprets a length starting with a newline, leading to a negative length and exception.

The failing test survivesBlankLinesInPaxHeader uses a tar archive that apparently contains blank lines in the PAX headers. When parsePaxHeaders tries to process these blank lines, the unchecked conversion of the newline character to an int length causes the exception.

Hence, the root cause is that parsePaxHeaders does not validate that characters read when parsing the length prefix are digits (0-9). It should check that each character is a digit before subtracting '0' and computing the length. Encountering a newline or non-digit should cause the method to handle this gracefully, for example by ignoring blank lines or breaking out of parsing, instead of proceeding with an invalid negative length.

This explains why the test fails and the exception occurs when blank lines appear in PAX headers. The method needs additional validation on characters read during length parsing and appropriate handling for blank lines.

Next, I will look for more detail about how parsePaxHeaders is invoked or tested, or check related utility methods if necessary.

Title: Diagnosis (extended)

Details: We see from getNextTarEntry() that when a PAX header entry is encountered (currEntry.isPaxHeader()), the paxHeaders() method is called. The paxHeaders method calls parsePaxHeaders(this) (line 444) passing the current TarArchiveInputStream instance (which is an InputStream) to parse the PAX headers. It then reads the next entry and applies the parsed headers.

The test uses getTestStream to create a TarArchiveInputStream from a test resource showing the bug ("/COMPRESS-355.tar"). The parsePaxHeaders reads from the input stream and expects the format "length keyword=value\n".

The bug occurs when an empty line (likely a newline by itself) appears in the PAX headers. In parsePaxHeaders, the code assumes characters before the space on a line are all digits representing length and does not check for non-digit characters like newline (ASCII 10). When encountering a newline, subtracting '0' results in a negative value and a negative array size when allocating the rest buffer.

This confirms that the root cause is missing validation in parsePaxHeaders on characters read while parsing length, leading to NegativeArraySizeException on blank lines in PAX headers. This causes the test failure when reading the test archive with blank lines.

Next step: I will confirm if the parsing loop properly handles digit check or if the internal loop can be improved by retrieving comments or inspecting the loop that reads the 'len' field.

The parsePaxHeaders method references the GNU tar manual about the PAX header format: https://www.gnu.org/software/tar/manual/html_section/tar_92.html#SEC188

This section describes PAX extended headers where each header line is "length keyword=value\n" with the length as a decimal ASCII number.

This confirms that the length field must be a decimal number. The current implementation reading this length integer at lines 456-495 must explicitly check that each character is a digit (between '0' and '9') before converting and adding to len.

Therefore, the missing validation of input characters as digits while parsing length is inconsistent with the spec and the linked documentation. This is likely the root cause for NegativeArraySizeException when an empty line (newline other than digit) appears.

Suggested fix is to add checks in parsePaxHeaders to ensure characters building the length are digits; if not, handle blank or malformed lines gracefully to avoid negative length and exceptions.

Diagnosis remains consistent with earlier findings.
Title: Diagnosis

Details: The parsePaxHeaders method is designed to parse PAX extended headers, where each header line begins with a decimal ASCII number indicating the length of the entry, followed by a space, then "keyword=value", and ends with a newline. The method reads character by character to construct the integer length. However, it does not check if each character is a digit before subtracting '0' to compute the length. When a blank line (newline character) is encountered, subtracting '0' yields a negative value, making the length negative. This negative length leads to a NegativeArraySizeException when allocating a byte array for the remaining header data. 

The test `survivesBlankLinesInPaxHeader` replicates this scenario by providing a tar archive with blank lines in the PAX headers. Hence, the bug is due to missing validation of digits while parsing the length field in parsePaxHeaders. The documentation referenced in the method comments agrees that the length must be a decimal ASCII number, so characters must be validated as digits. The method should detect non-digit characters like newline and handle such blank lines gracefully without throwing exceptions. This explains the test failure due to the exception, identifying the root cause in the parsePaxHeaders method's length parsing logic.
